posts.name: PePe QuiCoSE
posts.cooked:
phantaskippy: curious, with which heroes you do not have a high win rate?

About Argent/Expatriette: I'll say it's the other way around, Expatriette makes Argent better. Similar to how Zero makes Legacy better. Thing is, if Argent is with a guy who has no use for a buff, he doesn't get much out of his plays. OTOH, if his buff allows a hero to do double damage, he is great because although the other guy is dealing the damage, it's Argent who is doubling it. Since these guys can get more out of the buffs, they are increasing the importance of the buffer in the team. If I'm giving a guy a +1 damage and he uses it only once, my play was worth 1 damage, but if he uses it 5 times, my play was worth 5 damage. This is just to point out that Expat's power doesn't really change depending on her team since she doesn't affect other guys as much. I'm of the opinion that each Hero should be cool and fancy to play on his own without considering pairings, Villains or Terrains (though, I still love you Zero). I hold even that Ra makes Argent better than Expat, since Argent can also Vernal Sonata his Inferno/Fire Blast once set up.

I have tried several of the variants posted for Expat (and Fixer) and ended up sticking with one of my own (surprise surprise). Tried the "discard a card to keep an Ammon instead of destroying it" which I ditched on the 2nd turn: I was just emptying my hand to keep Hollow Rounds up. Tried "Ammo breaks on it's second use, tap it the first time you use it" which worked but... wasn't much fun or added much. Tried adding "draw a card" to Load which I found I still only wanted to use on the same occasions I wanted to use her regular power: for Pride/Prejudice/QuickDraw (if one gun was down), RPG Launcher and Unload. Tried the "do 0 damage and draw a card" and it's variations (you could play an ammo card there) which I forgot as soon as I got a good card down (ok, it solved the "I have no guns in hand" problem but became irrelevant way too fast).

That got me thinking on Expat's deck structure and how she feels to play (and how I think she should feel to play). I figured that while most heroes have a super set-up that they can aim for, besides doing stuff on the board, Expat only aims for Unload. That means having lots of guns down (that you won't be shooting) and hoping you even draw Unload. Speed Loading is great for Ammo but that's it (either with or without putting an Ammo card on top of your deck). She is a damage dealer who's base power is play cards, but she has no cards that deal damage upon being played (other than RPG).

Going on a tangent a bit, I realized that my idea of a gun-wielder hero (ala Punisher) would be a guy that get guns down FAST, use them, destroy them and get another one out just as fast. So I would have wanted something like guns of "One Hand" and "Two Hands" which would limit which ones you could have in play, and having guns destroy themselves, make you draw and play a new gun giving the feel that the guy/gal just burned through whatever he had in hand and went for the next gun. Expat feels more like getting an arsenal all aligned and hoping you get the clinch that fires all the guns with 1 click. And even then... Unload is not such an awesome card, not like other heroe's "ultimate" card. With all guns down and without Ammo it does 11 damage to 1 target. With Ammo it rises to 19 which is more impressive but takes almost twice as much to reach that. Damage increase are great because they are a +5 each, but at the same time damage reduction hurts as much. The fun/interesting decisions you have with Expat (IMO, of course) is when you have some guns down and you have to choose which Ammo is the best for which gun this turn. Yeah, usually is just Hollow Rounds on Shotgun, but when you dont have that, or you do but you are giving up on Liquid Nitrogen on SubMachine gun.

So what I wanted was a way to help her get to her ultimate set up while contributing, matching her damage-dealer role without one-shot damage cards and making her base power a bit more interesting. I just accepted the fact that you could have games where you just couldn't draw a gun. In every case, the previous variants were just a tad lacking in one of the areas.

TL:DR

The variant I'm using is: every Ammo card reads "When this enters play you may draw a card". I'm pretty sure this looks quite silly after a wall of text but that's the variant that has really worked. It helps you get the damage for the turn up while also helping cylce your deck. Increases your hand size which ends up with more options each turn and having harder decisions on what to play. Makes Speed Loading from great to awesome. Makes the Pride/Prejudice extra Ammo slot desirable for Ammo cards you don't care to use right now and want to see other cards. Basically, so far it has made Expat feels her stand on her own and have a more 'build-up' feel instead of 'let's just shoot Tactical shotgun again'.

One variant rule I've kicked around with her for fun is when Expat destroys a target with a power she may draw a card or use an additional power.

Some variations I've tried:

1.  Concealed Carrier - Power:  Reveal cards from the top of your deck until a gun card is revealed, put it into play, shuffle your deck.

That gets you a random gun anytime you want one.  It is alright, not a fan myself, but then I'm a Vegas All-Star at Expat, so I never used it (much like Load)

This one I like, no cost for her pistols, which is cool since they are her signature cards, she also recovers from equip destruction insanely fast.  It makes her a bit more powerful, but not much, those pistols don't beat an Assault Rifle or Shotgun most games, it just lowers her fail rate.  Starting hand has one of the pistols or quick draw makes for a great start.

If your opening hand contains no guns, you may put it on the bottom of your deck and draw 4 new cards.

That burns 20% of your deck, turning the rare "no guns for 3 rounds" game into an insanely rare occurance.

 

I like the Lock and Load option a lot though, I will try it out.

posts.cooked:
There are a few heores that have their base power immediately replaced (e.g. Wraith), so, to me at least, not using at all the time isn't a big deal. However, you are right. There are very few times that it is worth it to play an Ammo card for Load, then use the gun the next turn. All of the guns do the same exact or more damage by using their power twice isntead of Loading an Ammo and using a power The notable exception is Submachine Gun with Hollow Points. This of course assumes that you can't just play the Ammo during your second play phase.

Now, when do I use it? When I can't destroy a target in one round with the heroes help. This isn't always true, but sometimes it helps.

For example, if you are playing against Voss and you have Assault Rifle and Incediary Rounds in your hand. Assasult Rifle itself won't destroy anything without help. Assuming you don't have other heroes dealing damage, you have two options.

1) Turn 1: Play Assault Rifle and use it's power. Turn 2: Play Whatever then use Assault Rifle to destroy three targets.

2) Turn 1: Play Assault Rifle and Incendiary Rounds (or Hollow Points if the Guard is in play). Turn 2: Play Whatever then use Assault Rifle to destroy 3 targets.

The advantage of #2 over #1 is that you can hit new targets that come into play, assuming there weren't three targets to hit to begin with.

This, of course, will depend on the villains and the damage power of the other heroes, but playing the Ammo on turn #1 to destroy new targets on turn #2 can be beneficial.

Of course, all of this assumes that you can't destroy targets in one round, and that you can't play the Ammo card during turn #1's play phase. Are these situations very specific, sure, but take advantage of whatever you can.
